decisive_spans.text: an asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin groove on the left side of his forehead, frontal scalp, and vertex area
Image D: High-power view shows inflammatory infiltrates between adipocytes with hyaline fat necrosis in the subcutis

response.rationale: The patient presents with an asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin groove on the forehead and scalp, which is a key feature of Morphea. Histopathological findings of inflammatory infiltrates between adipocytes with hyaline fat necrosis in the subcutis further support Morphea. While Discoid lupus erythematosus has some supporting features, the negative ANA and anti-dsDNA antibodies, along with the absence of systemic involvement, make it less likely. The direct immunofluorescence findings are somewhat ambiguous and can be seen in other conditions as well.
